request: I want a habit tracker. I can add habits, tick each one off for today, and see the last 7 days for each one, with a streak count. It should remember everything when I come back. I can delete a habit.
tuning: T1 (2026-10-30, after the first G4 and G2 runs, which both left "untick" out and failed B7): a mark a person can make, they can take back. The tick block always toggles, and "untick" leaves the actions menu. Every DeepSeek app built the undo unasked; in code it comes free with a toggle, and only the menu had made it a separate decision.

handover.note: Every page the scope agreed (docs/decisions/000-initial-scope.md) is built: the plan is done, so hand over now, in one message and no questions: what they own, what they can change in Studio themselves, that an editor can be built for them if Studio is too much, and how to come back. Say it from `theyOwn` and `comeBack`, the canon's words.
handover.theyOwn: When it's finished, the app is yours in a way code from an agency never is. The project is a folder of files on your computer. NodeGX Studio is installed beside it: an open-source editor for pages, elements, workflows and data. Change a heading, a font, a button colour or a translation yourself. It works without the AI. Nobody charges you for it or can take it away. If Studio itself is more than you want, ask your AI coder for an editor that matches how you think about your app, with only the things you change in it.
handover.comeBack: When you want more, come back. Ask for a contact form, or a members' area with payments. The files are a blueprint the AI reads, and the build was written down as it went, so it picks up where it left off.
handover.rule: When the plan is done, hand over: say what they own, what they can change in Studio themselves, that an editor can be built for them if Studio is too much, and how to come back.
